content.title: HIDDEN NUTRIENT WINNERS IN YOUR {{PRODUCE}} DRAWER
facts: **Raspberries** have nearly three times more **fiber** than strawberries, gram for gram.
**Kale** contains notably more **vitamin K** than spinach, even though both are dark leafy greens.
**Artichokes** pack about twice the **fiber** of broccoli per serving.
**Brussels sprouts** have several times more **vitamin K** than green beans.
**Pears** (eaten with the skin) offer roughly double the **fiber** of peaches.
**Swiss chard** contains dramatically more **vitamin K** than iceberg lettuce — it's not close.
**Passion fruit** has significantly more **fiber** than mango, despite being smaller.
**Parsley** is one of the richest sources of **vitamin K** of any common vegetable, far surpassing celery.
**Guava** has about twice the **fiber** of a banana, plus a fraction of the sugar.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
None of this means one fruit or veggie is 'bad' and another is 'good' — it just means some options quietly pack more of a specific nutrient than others. Your body's needs, digestion, and reactions to different foods are unique, so always pay attention to how you personally feel rather than chasing a single number on a label.
